title: Energy Audit Work Order Form
subtitle: An original energy audit workflow that controls authorized field work from dispatch through return to service, with explicit qualified-review, stop-work, escalation, and accountable handoff controls.
description: A workflow-complete energy audit work order form for the building energy-use assessment that captures exact identity, domain observations, supporting evidence, decisions, exceptions, responsible owners, and closeout without replacing professional judgment or the organization's controlling procedures.
use_case: Use when a qualified crew receives a defined task and must preserve asset identity, work limits, energy-control references, as-found evidence, work performed, testing, exceptions, and operations handoff. The energy assessment lead owns routing, and closure requires documented evidence, disposition of restrictions, and acceptance by the designated reviewer.

sections.title: Energy audit work order identity and dispatch
sections.guidance: Issue a traceable order with clear ownership, site contacts, and approved work limits.

sections.title: Energy audit asset context, scope, and resources
sections.guidance: Match the order to the exact building energy-use assessment and define work that is included and excluded.

blocks.label: Authorized task scope
items: Reconcile utility accounts, meters, fuels, and baseline periods
Confirm facility use, occupancy, weather, and production drivers
Inventory envelope, HVAC, lighting, water, and process systems
Observe schedules, setpoints, sequences, and representative loads
Collect non-invasive measurements under an approved measurement plan
Normalize or annotate material baseline anomalies
Screen opportunities with assumptions, dependencies, and uncertainty
Identify comfort, ventilation, reliability, and operational constraints
Assign data gaps and technical questions to qualified reviewers
Prepare findings, evidence index, and implementation handoff

blocks.label: Scope, exclusions, parts, and completion criteria

fields.label: Approved work, explicit exclusions, required parts or tools, evidence expected, and completion criteria

sections.title: Energy audit pre-work controls and authorization
sections.guidance: Do not begin intrusive work until hazards, system effects, isolation ownership, and test authority are explicit.

blocks.label: Pre-work authorization confirmations
items: Exact asset, boundaries, sources, and affected systems were identified
Site-specific procedure and applicable requirements were reviewed
Authorized and affected people, roles, and communications were confirmed
Electrical, mechanical, pressure, thermal, chemical, gravity, and stored energy were assessed
Isolation devices and personal or group controls remain under designated ownership
Stored or residual energy was controlled and verification evidence was recorded
Test or temporary re-energization steps and authority are explicit
Public, customer, traffic, environmental, and critical-load controls are in place

blocks.label: Energy-control and qualified-person boundary
blocks.guidance: An energy audit is an evidence record, not permission to open equipment, change controls, or perform hazardous testing. Use non-invasive observations unless an approved task, qualified person, suitable instrument, and site procedure control the work. Stop when conditions or system effects differ from the approved plan and route the issue for professional review. This work order records references and decisions; it does not replace the site's energy-control procedure. Unknown, changed, or reaccumulating energy is a stop condition until the designated authorized person re-establishes and verifies control.

sections.title: Energy audit work execution and test evidence
sections.guidance: Record what was actually done, by whom, against which task, and with what result.

blocks.label: As-left readings and test results
blocks.guidance: Record method, instrument, operating state, and acceptance reference in linked evidence when needed.

fields.label: Unexpected conditions, approved changes, temporary measures, test context, and evidence links

sections.title: Energy audit exceptions, stop conditions, and escalation
sections.guidance: Make every unresolved condition visible with an immediate control, owner, due point, and final disposition.

blocks.label: Stop-condition screen
items: Exposed electrical parts or a panel requiring intrusive access
Unsafe roof, ladder, mechanical-room, or confined-space access
Moving machinery, hot surface, steam, pressure, or rotating equipment
Suspected hazardous material, severe moisture, or poor air condition
Measurement would disrupt a critical process or life-safety system
Instrument rating, method, or authorization is not confirmed
Site condition differs materially from the approved measurement plan
Any observation requires work outside the assessor's competence or scope
blocks.guidance: Check any condition observed or reported; checking an item does not mean the condition is controlled.

blocks.label: Qualified-person and stop-work boundary
blocks.guidance: An energy audit is an evidence record, not permission to open equipment, change controls, or perform hazardous testing. Use non-invasive observations unless an approved task, qualified person, suitable instrument, and site procedure control the work. Stop when conditions or system effects differ from the approved plan and route the issue for professional review.

blocks.label: Exception and escalation register
blocks.guidance: Link each work order exception to supporting evidence and keep it open until disposition is recorded.

sections.title: Energy audit decision, handoff, and accountable closeout
sections.guidance: Record the decision, remaining limitations, next action, and the people accountable for acceptance.

blocks.label: Closeout completeness
items: Building energy-use assessment identity and location were reconciled
Observed facts, measurements, and evidence references are complete
Decision authority and applicable review requirements were confirmed
Stop conditions, restrictions, and open exceptions remain visible
Customer, operations, or site handoff was recorded
Next action, owner, due point, and record-retention route are explicit

fields.label: Limitations, assumptions, restrictions, customer message, and next-action context

blocks.label: Accountable review and handoff
blocks.guidance: Signatures acknowledge the recorded decision and handoff; they do not waive unresolved restrictions.
